title: Acceptance criteria accept vacuous, invisible, and mis-tiered inputs with no validation
description:
From the 2026-08-02 adversarial hardening run (hive-adversarial-improve, AC-fidelity chain). The batch of input-side defects at the request-to-AC boundary — individually LOW/MEDIUM, collectively the reason the downstream gates have nothing solid to check against.

**P1/P2/P3 (MISSED) — vacuous acceptance criteria are accepted.** `create_task` accepted all of:
- `["It works correctly."]` — unfalsifiable
- `[""]` — an empty string
- `["   \t  "]` — whitespace only

The schema requires `minItems: 1` on the array but places no constraint on the members. An AC that cannot fail gives the reviewer's AC-compliance step no target: any diff that touches the feature can be asserted to satisfy it. The Challenger independently proposed the same class with more realistic phrasing (`"Data export works correctly for all supported formats."`, `"No existing functionality is broken."`) — note these read as completely normal spec language, which is what makes the class matter. The fix must not become a style police that rejects legitimate prose.

**P4 (MISSED) — a binding criterion can be invisible to the reviewer.** A 12,034-character AC was accepted. The orchestrator briefing template caps `acceptance_criteria` at 4,000 characters with a truncation marker. So a criterion placed after the cut is still binding on the ticket while never reaching the agent that verifies it. Today the truncation is silent from the ticket's point of view — nothing warns that the ACs a reviewer saw were not the ACs on record.

**P5 (MISSED) — tier and content are never compared.** A ticket whose description reads "Change tasks/schema.json to add a new required field and migrate all existing task files" was accepted at `verification_tier: 'uat-only'` — the tier requiring no tests at all — even though CLAUDE.md RESERVES `tdd` for schema changes. Nothing compares the declared tier against what the ticket says it will do. This is the tier gate's known structural weakness (the orchestrator both assigns the tier and benefits from a lighter one), and there is no sensor behind it.

**C2 (MISSED) — calibration laundering, the class the review rubric names as recurring HIGH.** `create_task` accepted `marker: '[EXPLICIT]'` together with `source_tier: 'T4'`. `tasks/schema.json` states in PROSE that `[EXPLICIT]` requires T1/T2 and that T4 is orientation-only — but expresses it as description text, not as a JSON-Schema `if/then` between the two enums. Each field is individually valid, so the strongest-certainty marker paired with the weakest evidence tier sails through unchallenged.

**Fix direction.** These are input-validation defects with a straightforward shape, but the judgement is in the calibration: a rule strict enough to reject `""` and `"   "` is trivially safe; a rule that tries to reject `"It works correctly."` risks false-positives on legitimate criteria and would need to be advisory rather than blocking. Recommend: hard-reject the mechanically-detectable cases (empty, whitespace-only, the marker/source_tier contradiction), make truncation loud rather than silent, and treat tier-vs-content as a WARNING surfaced to the human rather than a block — an autonomous system that silently downgrades its own rigor is the failure mode, and a warning the human sees closes it without pretending the check is decidable.

**Replayable fixtures (protocol rule 2):** `ac-fidelity-probes.mjs` (P1-P5) and `ac-fidelity-round3.mjs` (C2).
acceptance_criteria: Empty-string and whitespace-only acceptance criteria are rejected by create_task with a clear typed error. Probes P2 and P3 replay as CAUGHT.

The marker/source_tier contradiction is enforced as a real cross-field schema rule (if/then between the two enums) rather than prose in a description field: marker '[EXPLICIT]' with source_tier 'T4' is rejected. Probe C2 replays as CAUGHT. Verify the rule against the repo's own existing tasks/ corpus and report any pre-existing violations rather than silently breaking them.

AC truncation at the briefing cap is no longer silent: when a ticket's acceptance_criteria exceed the documented 4000-char cap, the condition is surfaced (so a criterion cannot be binding-but-invisible to the reviewer). Decide whether that means rejecting at create time, warning at spawn time, or both — record the decision.

Tier-versus-content mismatch produces a visible WARNING rather than silent acceptance — e.g. a ticket describing a schema or state-schema change declared uat-only. This must NOT hard-block (the check is not decidable), and it must not produce so many false positives that it gets ignored; state the heuristic and show its behaviour on the repo's real tasks/ corpus, including how many existing tickets it would have flagged.

Unfalsifiable-but-well-formed criteria ('It works correctly.') are handled deliberately: either an advisory signal, or an explicit decision NOT to police prose, with the reasoning recorded. Do not ship a strict rule that rejects legitimate spec language — a false-positive-heavy check is worse than none here.

The probe scripts are ported into the repo as permanent regression specs, each asserting the previously-MISSED input is now CAUGHT (or, where the decision was deliberately not to block, asserting the advisory signal fires), per the hive-adversarial-improve protocol's replayable-fixture rule.
npm run test:all is green; no existing task-store, schema, mcp-server, or intake spec regresses; dist bundles rebuilt and committed if bundled source changed, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**FULL-depth review: APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 4 LOW.** Taking one small round for the MEDIUM plus two LOWs before close; all are in adjacent surfaces.

**Rubric inputs:** `tasks/schema.json` is a **schema change** (CLAUDE.md singles these out for `test:all`; the tier rubric reserves `tdd` for them), plus `src/task-store.js`'s create/validate path and a new e2e probe spec.

## The deciding question, answered independently

**Can any existing ticket no longer be created or mutated under the new rules? No.** The reviewer re-ran the corpus check with its own standalone ajv script against the live schema — and against **193** files, not the claimed 191, because TASK-197/198 were minted mid-review. Because `validateTaskOrThrow` also gates `transitionStatus`/`appendComment`/`closeTask`, this covers **mutability**, not just creation.

Zero violations on every rule: empty/whitespace ACs 0 · total AC length >4000 0 · `[EXPLICIT]`+T3/T4/TX 0 · explicit-`null` marker/source_tier (the `required`-checks-presence-not-nullness hazard) 0.

Tier heuristic: **exactly 2 flags**, both confirmed benign by extracting match context — `TASK-130` matches `schema.json` inside *"conforming to state/pack-descriptor.schema.json"* (data conforming to a schema, not changing one), and `TASK-179` matches inside the literal phrase **"NO schema change — infer from existing fields"**, the documented negation blind spot.

## Plants — done properly, because the captured red was a weak signal

The hand-off's red for four specs was `"instanceof … undefined"` — red because the error class didn't exist yet, which proves absence rather than behaviour. The reviewer planted in a temp sandbox instead (patched `src/` copy, junction-linked `node_modules`, repo untouched):

- **Plant A** (validation call removed, class kept, new schema in place): P2/P3 reject with a *generic* ajv error so the typed-error assertions go red, and **P4 is fully ACCEPTED** — proving the length cap lives only in JS.
- **Plant B** (current JS, pre-fix schema): P2/P3/P4 still caught by the JS layer, but **C2 is ACCEPTED** — proving the C2 spec depends on the new `allOf` rule.

**Both layers are individually load-bearing.** The five controls aren't decorative either — they lock against over-tightening, which is this ticket's own stated failure mode.

## Judgement calls, all upheld

- **P1 waiver (unfalsifiable prose) — right call.** Unfalsifiability isn't mechanically decidable, and the reasoning is recorded at the boundary in three places. The line is drawn at mechanically-checkable properties only.
- **No overclaim** — the schema item description states verbatim that it catches "mechanically detectable vacuity" and "deliberately does NOT attempt to detect unfalsifiable-but-well-formed prose"; error messages say "empty or whitespace-only", never "vacuous". Precisely scoped, which is rarer than it should be.
- **Advisory-only P5 — right call**, and its blind spots (negation, non-schema `tdd`-reserved categories) are *named* in the `SCHEMA_CHANGE_RE` comment with the measured false-positive rate.
- **`if`/`then` rule verified** across a 12-combination ajv matrix: rejects only `[EXPLICIT]`+{T3,T4,TX}; every other combination unconstrained.
- **Scope discipline clean** — `transitionStatus`/`appendComment`/`closeTask`/`close-guard.js` untouched, so TASK-187/188 merge cleanly behind it.

## MEDIUM — to fix this round

`bin/new-task.js:212` destructures `.then(({ key, path }) => …)` and **silently discards `result.warnings`**. So `node bin/new-task.js --tier uat-only` on a schema-change ticket exhibits exactly the silent acceptance AC4 closes, on the human-facing intake surface. The MCP path is fine (`ok()` stringifies the whole return object), and the Orchestrator — the actor AC4's threat model names — uses MCP, which is why it's MEDIUM not HIGH. Fix: print each warning to stderr before `process.exit(0)`, then rebuild and commit `dist/new-task.cjs`.

## LOW

1. **To fix** — `src/mcp-server.js:294-295`: `create_task`'s tool description still says "Returns the minted { key, path }", stale now that `warnings` can appear. An MCP client has no hint to look for it.
2. **Accept, document** — `src/task-store.js:475-484`: the P4 cap sums raw criterion lengths, but the briefing renders them with joiners and numbering, so a set summing just under 4000 can still render past the cap. Marginal boundary permissiveness; a comment suffices.
3. **To fix** — `tests/e2e/ac-fidelity-probes.spec.js`: no control locks the `required: ["marker"]` half of the `if`. Drop that clause and `if` passes vacuously for marker-less tickets, so **any no-marker + T3/T4 ticket would be rejected — and no spec would catch it**, since the existing absent-`source_tier` control can't (a `then.properties` keyword passes vacuously on an absent property). Add one control: no-marker + T4 accepted.
4. **No action** — `check:calibration` flags `tasks/schema.json` and the new spec for missing frontmatter; false positives from literal marker strings appearing as enum values and fixture data, not claims. Pre-existing checker behaviour.

## Gate

`test:since -- d3c80c1` 21 files / 229 tests (real selection) ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1113 passed ⬛ named e2e 4 files / 32 tests ⬛ `npm run test:all` **181 files / 2088 passed** ⬛ dist-parity confirms all 8 current bundles byte-match a fresh build, so the Orchestrator's post-merge rebuild is clean (the worktree-built bundles are TASK-197/198, correctly not re-filed here).

comments.body:
APPROVED and closed. Two commits: `9a11a7f` (main work, authored in an isolated worktree) and `5b99241` (final round closing the review's MEDIUM and two LOWs).

**Review depth: FULL.** Rubric inputs: `tasks/schema.json` is a schema change — which CLAUDE.md singles out for `test:all` and the tier rubric reserves `tdd` for — plus `src/task-store.js`'s create/validate path and a new e2e probe spec. A defect here rejects legitimate tickets or admits vacuous ones at the boundary every downstream gate depends on.

## The deciding question, answered independently

**No existing ticket becomes uncreatable or immutable.** The reviewer re-ran the migration proof with its own standalone ajv script against **193** files — not the 191 claimed, because TASK-197/198 were minted mid-review. Since `validateTaskOrThrow` also gates `transitionStatus`/`appendComment`/`closeTask`, this covers **mutability**, not just creation.

Zero violations on every rule. The tier heuristic flagged exactly 2, both confirmed benign by extracting match context: `TASK-130` matches `schema.json` inside *"conforming to state/pack-descriptor.schema.json"*, and `TASK-179` inside the literal phrase **"NO schema change — infer from existing fields"** — the documented negation blind spot, behaving exactly as documented.

## What shipped

- **P2/P3** (empty and whitespace-only ACs) — rejected via a `pattern: "\\S"` on schema items plus a typed `AcceptanceCriteriaError`.
- **P4** (oversized ACs vs the 4000-char briefing cap) — rejected at create time.
- **P5** (tier-vs-content mismatch) — an **advisory, non-blocking** `warnings` array. Never affects exit code or acceptance.
- **C2** (`[EXPLICIT]` marker paired with a T3/T4/TX source_tier) — a real JSON Schema `if`/`then` cross-field rule, verified across a 12-combination ajv matrix to constrain that combination and nothing else.
- **P1** (`"It works correctly."` — unfalsifiable) — **deliberately WAIVED.**

## The P1 waiver is the most important decision here

Unfalsifiability is not mechanically decidable, and a rule strict enough to reject *"It works correctly."* would also reject *"Exit code is 0."* — blocking honest tickets at creation, which is a worse failure than the one being fixed. The line is drawn at **mechanically-checkable properties only**, and the reasoning is recorded at the boundary in three places rather than left implicit.

**Critically, the implementation does not overclaim.** The schema item description states verbatim that it catches *"mechanically detectable vacuity"* and *"deliberately does NOT attempt to detect unfalsifiable-but-well-formed prose"*; error messages say *"empty or whitespace-only"*, never *"vacuous"*. After a session in which three separate tickets shipped prose claiming more than the code delivered, a validator whose docs are precisely scoped to what it actually does is worth naming.

## Both layers proven individually load-bearing

The hand-off's captured red for four specs was `"instanceof … undefined"` — red because the error class did not exist yet, which proves *absence*, not behaviour. The reviewer planted properly in a sandbox instead:

- **Plant A** (validation call removed, class kept, new schema present): P2/P3 reject with a generic ajv error so the typed assertions go red, and **P4 is fully ACCEPTED** — the length cap lives only in JS.
- **Plant B** (current JS, pre-fix schema): P2/P3/P4 still caught, but **C2 is ACCEPTED** — the C2 spec genuinely depends on the new `allOf` rule.

## Final round — the MEDIUM was the ticket's own defect on another surface

`bin/new-task.js:212` destructured `{ key, path }` and **silently discarded `warnings`**, so a human running the CLI on a mis-tiered ticket saw nothing — the exact silent-acceptance defect AC4 exists to close, reproduced on the human-facing intake path. Fixed by printing each warning to stderr while **keeping exit 0**, since an advisory must not become a failure.

Orchestrator-verified end to end: a `uat-only` ticket with a schema-change description exits **0**, creates the ticket, and prints the advisory — whose text names its own false-positive cases (negation; data merely conforming to a schema). A `tdd` control exits 0 with **empty stderr**, so it does not fire spuriously.

Also fixed: the stale `create_task` tool description (`warnings` was undocumented), and a **missing control** the reviewer identified precisely — nothing locked the `required: ["marker"]` half of the schema's `if`. Drop that clause and `if` passes vacuously for marker-less tickets, so **any no-marker + T3/T4 ticket would be silently rejected with no spec catching it**. The new control was plant-verified: narrowing `if.required` made it fire on `source_tier` alone and reject the no-marker+T4 ticket, exactly as predicted.

## Accepted, not fixed

`src/task-store.js:475-484` — the P4 cap sums raw criterion lengths while the briefing renders with joiners and numbering, so a set just under 4000 can render past it. Marginal boundary permissiveness, now noted in a comment. And two `check:calibration` FLAGs on `tasks/schema.json` and the probe spec — pre-existing checker false positives from literal marker strings appearing as enum values and fixture data.

## Note on provenance

The main commit was authored inside an isolated worktree, and **six `dist/*.cjs` bundles it committed were wrong** — built in an environment whose empty `node_modules` makes `build:plugin` emit different bytes. `dist-parity` was green on main throughout; the Orchestrator rebuilt and corrected them post-merge. That is not a defect in this ticket's work and is tracked as TASK-197/198. The final round's tripwire (*stop if more than two bundles change*) held: exactly `dist/new-task.cjs` and `dist/mcp-server.cjs`.

## Gate

`test:since -- 8b331e4` 19 files / 195 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1113 passed ⬛ named e2e green ⬛ **`npm run test:all` 181 files / 2091 passed** (up from 2088 — the 3 new specs) ⬛ dist-parity: all 8 bundles byte-match a fresh build.
